title: Latent Sky event catalogue
description:
The top-level index the web app loads FIRST, before any manifest. It answers one question — which events exist and which one opens by default — and nothing else. Every heavier fact (frames, layers, ranges, identity) stays in manifest.schema.json, which this file deliberately does not duplicate or summarise beyond the single `hasHero`/`kind` capability bit the switcher needs to label an entry before fetching it.

Producer: pipeline/src/latentsky/catalogue.py, which DERIVES kind/hasHero by inspecting each referenced manifest — never by being told. Consumer: web/, which fetches /data/web/catalogue.json, resolves the chosen entry's `manifest` against the catalogue URL, and then loads it exactly as it does today.

Adding an event is a data change: append an entry, move `default`. The two planned heroes are already expressible — Taiwan (SFNO -> CorrDiffTaiwan) and the March 2025 US tornado outbreak (StormCast, region `conus`).

schemaVersion.description: Independent of the manifest's schemaVersion. The app must be able to read the catalogue even if it then rejects a manifest version it does not know.

events.description: Display order IS array order — the switcher renders top to bottom as given, so the pipeline controls sequencing without the app sorting on anything. A one-entry catalogue is valid and is the pre-hero state: the app must degrade to no switcher at all rather than showing a control with one option.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identity, unique across the catalogue (uniqueness is gated by the builder — JSON Schema cannot express it). Suitable for a ?event= URL parameter and for persisting a viewer's choice. Conventionally equal to the referenced manifest's run.id, but not required to be: the catalogue is display metadata and the manifest is the data contract.

title.description: The switcher's primary line, e.g. "Global — Typhoon Gaemi week".

subtitle.description: One honest line naming what the data actually is, e.g. "ERA5 reanalysis, 0.5°". Not marketing: this is where the scientific-honesty posture of §13 starts, before the viewer has loaded anything.

manifest.description: Path to the event's manifest, relative to THIS file — resolve with new URL(manifest, catalogueUrl). The pattern forbids absolute paths, protocol-relative paths, drive letters and ".." segments (every segment must start alphanumeric), so a catalogue can never point the app outside its own data tree.

kind.description: What the event can show. "hero" means the manifest carries at least one hero-fine layer, so the coarse/fine reveal exists; "global-only" means it does not and the app must not offer a reveal affordance. DERIVED from the manifest by the pipeline.

region.description: Grouping and labelling key for the switcher — not a bounding box (the manifest's layer rects are authoritative for geometry). The enum is closed on purpose so a typo cannot silently create an ungrouped event; all three planned events are already covered.

hasHero.description: The capability bit the UI branches on, locked equal to kind by the if/then rules below. Redundant with kind by design — kind names the event, hasHero is the boolean a component reads — and the schema makes the redundancy unable to become an inconsistency. DERIVED from the manifest by the pipeline.

default.description: The event that opens when no choice is expressed. Exactly one entry in the array must be true — enforced here by minContains/maxContains as well as in the builder, because a hand-edited catalogue reaches the browser without the builder.
